title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets' (loop relation). It is his version of the defining relations of what is now called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, worked out at the level of GL(2,Ẑ), i.e. the congruence completion of the modular group. Notation: rho is an elliptic element of order 3 (order 6 in GL2), sigma_inf is an elliptic element of order 4, eps_0 = sigma_inf.rho is the parabolic (translation) generator, tau_inf is a reflection, and mu is a unit of Ẑ. On the previous page Grothendieck shows that the loop relation xi = eps.eta.l^nu (with xi = alpha rho(alpha)^-1 and eta = beta sigma_inf(beta)^-1) is equivalent to two conditions. The first is that the two matrices delta.alpha(c rho + d) and beta(t sigma_inf + u) tau_inf^{alpha_2} coincide; both are upper triangular, equal to (1 B; 0 D). The second is mu D = 1. He then defines the Borel element u_{alpha,beta} = (1 0; 0 1)-normalised matrix (mu, mu B; 0, 1). It equals mu.delta.alpha.(c rho + d) and also mu.beta.(t sigma_inf + u).tau^{alpha_2}. On this page he introduces a third parameter f in SL(2,Ẑ) and sets u_{alpha,beta,f} = f^{-1} u_{alpha,beta} (formula 79). This yields alpha_0 = f^{-1} alpha and beta_0 = f^{-1} beta. He then records the conjugation formulas, with u(s) = u s u^{-1}. (80): u_{alpha,beta,f}(sigma_inf) = int(beta_0)(sigma_inf) and u_{alpha,beta,f}(rho) = int(alpha_0)(rho). For f = 1 these become (81), which he notes follow trivially from the two expressions (78): the factors (c rho + d) and (t sigma_inf + u) lie in the centralisers of rho and sigma_inf, and tau_inf at most inverts sigma_inf. (80) is completed by (82): u_{alpha,beta,f}(eps_0) = eps.int(f^{-1})(eps_0^mu), which for f = 1 gives (83): u_{alpha,beta}(eps_0) = eps.eps_0^mu. Since eps_0 = sigma_inf rho, this unwinds to int(beta)(sigma_inf).int(alpha)(rho) = eps.eps_0^mu. The next page checks this against the loop relation, using eta.sigma_inf(xi) = eps.l_0^nu. In modern terms: a pair (alpha, beta) satisfying the loop relation acts on the generators sigma_inf and rho by 'local' conjugations. On the congruence completion GL(2,Ẑ), that action is realised by one global inner automorphism, namely conjugation by the Borel matrix (mu *; 0 1). It sends the parabolic generator to ±(its mu-th power), which is the familiar picture of a cyclotomic-type character acting on the cusp. The illegible right-margin note seems to say that int(u_{alpha,beta,f}) therefore does better than / is compatible with some action (of 𝔖_3 or a Γ_{0,3}-type group?) and relates SL(2,Ẑ) to SL(3,Ẑ). It cannot be read reliably.
errors: No substantive error visible. The step tau_inf^{alpha_2} sigma_inf tau_inf^{-alpha_2} = sigma_inf^{±1} can introduce a sign (sigma_inf^{-1} = -sigma_inf in GL2). Grothendieck absorbs this through eps = eps_2 and the convention fixing alpha_2. His subsequent remark (next page) says the formulas hold without sign ambiguity once alpha, beta, f are chosen. This sign bookkeeping is not fully checked on this page.
In (82) the factor int(f_*^{-1}) is somewhat ambiguous as written (f_* versus f). It should be read as conjugation by f^{-1}, consistent with (79).

ideas.what: Realising the action of a solution (alpha, beta) of the loop equation on the generators rho, sigma_inf of the modular group by a single inner automorphism of GL(2,Ẑ), given by an explicit upper-triangular (Borel) matrix u = (mu, muB; 0, 1)
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT / Gal(Q̄/Q) on the congruence completion SL2(Ẑ) through conjugation by a Borel element with cyclotomic diagonal entry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard: Galois action on the Tate module / congruence quotient via GL2 with cyclotomic determinant. In the GT setting, the actions on the profinite modular group are studied by Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto.
ideas.where_published: Material on the 'équation des lacets' is in La Longue Marche (1981) only in sketch form; this explicit computation is not in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Conjugation formulas u(sigma_inf) = int(beta)(sigma_inf), u(rho) = int(alpha)(rho), u(eps_0) = eps.eps_0^mu, and their f-twisted versions
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of a GT-type automorphism with the elliptic and parabolic generators (inertia at the cusp raised to the power lambda)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; the modular-group version Lochak–Schneps (1990s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck produces an explicit, sign-careful parametrisation of the solutions of the loop equation in GL(2,Ẑ) by a canonical Borel element u_{alpha,beta}. It depends only on alpha (and on beta only through a sign), with an extra SL2-parameter f. This is a concrete bookkeeping device, but its content (the congruence-level action is conjugation by diag(chi,1) up to a unipotent) is known.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck checking the GL2(Ẑ)-level shadow of the loop relation in detail, years before Drinfeld/Ihara-style formalism.

missed.claim: The illegible margin note seems to link the inner automorphism int(u_{α,β,f}) to some action (𝔖_3 or a Γ_{0,3}-type group) and to SL(3,Ẑ). A link with SL3 would be a non-standard direction, but the text is too illegible to assert anything.
missed.quote: ceci implique que int(u_{α,β,f}) a, mieux [?] ... Sl(2,Ẑ) ... Sl(3,Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If it really proposes extending the loop-equation analysis to SL3 or higher-rank congruence quotients, that would be a lead to check against the full manuscript; currently speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification page: explicit conjugation formulas showing that solutions of the loop equation act on GL(2,Ẑ) by conjugation with an upper-triangular matrix carrying the 'cyclotomic' unit mu. Historically nice as unpublished GT-prehistory detail, but mathematically standard; the only possibly unusual element (the SL3 margin remark) is illegible.
transcription_corrections: Right margin is very hard to read. Plausible reading: 'ceci implique que int(u_{α,β,f}) a, mieux [comme il se doit?], que l'[action] de u de 𝔊_{0,3}[?] ... des formules ... Sl(2,Ẑ)' ... 'Sl(3,Ẑ)'. The symbol transcribed as 𝔖_3 may be a Γ̂_{0,3}/𝔊_{0,3}-type symbol.
In (82) the struck-out text after the equals sign is followed by 'ε int(f_*^{-1})(ε_0^μ)'. The parenthetical reads '(où ε = ε_2 ∈ {±1})'.
Final word on the page is probably 'juste' or 'justes' (confirming the formula). The struck word below it is illegible.
The page number '399' at top is Grothendieck's own pagination; '199' at bottom is the archive scan number.
